payload.summary: The pinned repository (commit 36bd908b4f38e9ea8ca1a3ee6caaf71d405faf86) is the official ROCKET code by Dempster, Petitjean and Webb. It implements random convolutional kernels (code/rocket_functions.py: generate_kernels, apply_kernels producing PPV and max features per kernel) and the UCR experiment driver code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py. The driver uses RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=np.logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True), defaults to 10,000 kernels and 10 runs, and reports the mean test accuracy over runs as accuracy_mean. Data are read from the fixed UCR *_TRAIN.txt and *_TEST.txt files, so the fixed split is used. ECG200 is in the bake-off dataset list (.preprint/reproduce_experiments_bakeoff.py). The claimed method, dataset, split, and metric all map to official code here. No values are reported here.

entrypoints.why: UCR driver: loads the fixed TRAIN/TEST txt files, runs N runs (default 10) of 10,000 ROCKET kernels with RidgeClassifierCV, and writes accuracy_mean per dataset to results_ucr.csv.
Kernel generation (generate_kernels) and feature extraction (apply_kernels, PPV and max per kernel) used by the driver.
Preprint-era bake-off script that also lists ECG200; a second reference for the same experiment.

metricSources.description: Computes the per-run test accuracy with classifier.score(X_test_transform, Y_test) over num_runs runs and stores the mean as accuracy_mean. It is printed and written to results_ucr.csv.
Saved output file with the ECG200 accuracy_mean row. Recorded from the original run and not recomputed here.

payload.runInstructions: Obtain the UCR 2018 archive's Univariate_arff/ ECG200 TRAIN and TEST txt files. Install Python with numpy, pandas, numba, and scikit-learn (no requirements file exists in the repository). Create a dataset list file containing the single line ECG200. Run: python code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py -d ecg200.txt -i <parent dir of ECG200 folder> -o ./ -n 10 -k 10000. Read accuracy_mean for ECG200 from the output results_ucr.csv. Run from the code/ directory so rocket_functions.py imports correctly.
warnings: No dependency file (requirements, pyproject, lockfile) exists in the repository. The environment must be inferred from the imports (numpy, pandas, numba, scikit-learn) and the README.
The script passes normalize=True to RidgeClassifierCV. This argument was removed in newer scikit-learn releases, so an older scikit-learn version may be needed to run it unchanged.

The UCR data files are not in the repository and must be obtained separately. The script's variable-length and missing-value notes say these were interpolated or padded per the 2018 archive version, so the archive version matters.
The repository's saved ECG200 values are not used in this map. Whether they match the reviewed claim is left for the reproduction step.
The random seed is not set in the driver, so the mean over 10 runs will vary from run to run.

supervisorProposal.rationale: The board shows the pipeline got through ingestion, paper analysis, repository mapping (official ROCKET code, commit 36bd908, with the driver and RidgeClassifierCV setup matching the claim), and reconciliation. The plan was then refused by policy review: its command runs ../work/adapter/rocket_ecg200_runner.py, which is neither the repository entry point (code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py) nor the declared reviewed adapter (rocket-ecg200-runner). Preparation, execution, and review were all skipped, so no observation was produced and no metric value exists to compare with the paper's 0.906 ± 0.0053 target. Because nothing was measured, the evidence cannot support "not reproduced" or "reproduced"; "inconclusive" is the status it supports. A corrected plan that runs the declared adapter path or the official entry point could be re-attempted, but that work has not happened.
